A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated, revised, and added content.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendix C report original Gemma-2B experiments measuring token projections and hierarchical representation geometry.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original Gemma-2B and LLaMA-3-8B results, including projection measurements, intervention effects, and controlled comparisons of hierarchical geometry.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same whitening transformation and LDA representation estimator with Ledoit-Wolf covariance shrinkage in Equations 5.1–5.2. The added theoretical properties, comparator estimators, and evaluations do not change the proposed estimation procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds a limited intervention scenario testing target-versus-subordinate logit changes for three parent-child contrast pairs in Table 1; v1 empirically examined representation geometry. English WordNet noun/verb coverage and the curated animal/plant examples remain. Adding LLaMA changes model coverage rather than introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's random-word projection reference, v2 evaluates shuffled-unembedding controls in the retained WordNet analyses, random parent/grandparent assignments, a mean-vector estimator, and an unwhitened Euclidean alternative. Figures 3–5 and 10–12 substantially expand the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The reported train/test split changes from 80/20 to 70/30. v2 adds whole-token versus independently subsampled estimation, normalized-vector intervention tests, and LLaMA-3-8B noun evaluations. Hierarchy comparisons use inverse shortest-path distance instead of the earlier adjacency reference. These substantially revise and extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 tests whether apparent orthogonality arises from high dimensionality or token-set inclusion using random relatives, shuffled embeddings, and independent subsampling. Appendix F additionally tests mean estimation and removal of whitening. Table 1 adds intervention case studies. These analyses address alternative explanations largely untested in v1.

E5.justification: v1 Figures 4 and 9 report error bars of 1.96 times the standard error; the corresponding v2 projection analyses use standard deviation. Table 1 also reports standard deviation across token pairs. This changes statistical reporting, without establishing additional repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for interventions, controls, ablations, and LLaMA. For example, Table 1 reports a plant-to-animal intervention changing parent logit differences by 5.1265 ± 1.1731 and subordinate mammal-to-reptile differences by -0.0600 ± 1.2190. Revised projection plots use different splits, so they do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds Corollary 10 and a proof characterizing token projections onto categorical representation subspaces. Appendix G adds a Gaussian mean-vector derivation explaining inclusion-induced orthogonality. These extend the theoretical analysis. The earlier simplex theorem survives as Proposition 9, and the binary-contrast result is reorganized as Corollary 6 rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain vector representations for binary features, polytope representations for categorical concepts, and orthogonal structure for semantic hierarchy. v2 foregrounds polytopes, but v1 already defines them; its conditional simplex claim remains in v2 Appendix C. Additional model evidence supports the retained claims.

C2.justification: v1 interprets the observed geometry directly as evidence of semantic hierarchy. v2 explains how high-dimensional geometry and token-set inclusion can produce similar observations, distinguishes sibling from inclusion relationships, and interprets independent-subsampling controls. It also explains the empirical importance of LDA and the causal inner product, substantially refining the interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix E explicitly identifies displays using representations estimated from unsplit token collections, including retained visualizations. Projection captions also specify the normalized dot-product formula. These clarify implementation and reporting without establishing corresponding changes to previously unspecified settings. Existing preprocessing and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds the LLaMA-3 reference and removes several citations, including Patchscopes, Representation Engineering, and Ri et al.'s contrastive-loss work. It condenses the embedding-literature discussion while retaining the central positioning as an extension of Park et al.'s formalization.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten. The theoretical exposition is reorganized around binary and categorical vector representations; the simplex discussion and animal example move to appendices. The experimental narrative is restructured around representation existence, intervention, similarity, and controlled orthogonality tests.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the principal heatmap arrangement with shortest-distance, original-embedding, and shuffled-embedding panels, and introduces dedicated orthogonality line plots. Projection figures gain training curves and control panels. A numerical intervention table and additional analysis figures are added; the existing categorical visualization is relocated and its viewing angle revised.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support left high-dimensional geometry and token-set overlap as substantial alternative explanations. v2 directly investigates these through shuffled embeddings, random relatives, and independent subsampling, materially strengthening support for the central interpretation. Intervention measurements and LLaMA replication provide complementary validation. Changed splits and error-bar conventions prevent direct numerical improvement claims, but the stronger experimental controls constitute a substantial overall quality gain.
